CAMT is a plausible underfollowed backend-yield chokepoint candidate because HBM and advanced packaging increase inspection/metrology intensity.

US-listed pure-play memory backend OSAT exposure is limited; many direct beneficiaries such as Powertech are non-US-listed, so US-listed discovery may skew toward tools, inspection, test handlers, and materials rather than backend service providers.

summary: Layer 1B expansion found one direct US-listed OSAT reference anchor and three less obvious US-listed equipment/inspection/test beneficiaries tied to AI advanced packaging, HBM, GPU/accelerator test, and OSAT capacity. The strongest direct mapping is Amkor as an outsourced assembly/test provider with AI/HPC packaging exposure. The underfollowed lane is more interesting in specialty backend tools: Camtek for advanced packaging inspection/metrology, Cohu for HBM/GPU thermal handling and inspection/test, and Amtech as a small-cap speculative exception in reflow ovens used by OSATs for advanced packaging.
